references.text: The immediate fulfillment of God's decree in v. 26: God creates humankind in his image, as male and female.
Repeats that God created humankind in his likeness and links the creation account to Adam's genealogy.
Human dignity as beings created in God's image is used as the basis for the prohibition against murder.
Reflects on humanity's exalted position and dominion over creation, which was granted at creation.
James reminds us that humans are made in God's likeness (ὁμοίωσιν θεοῦ), corresponding directly to 'in our likeness' (כדמותנו).
Paul calls the man the image and glory of God, with a direct connection to the creation of humankind in God's image.
The new person is renewed according to their Creator's image—a restoration of the original image from creation.
The new person is created after God in true righteousness and holiness, reflecting creation in God's image.
Quotes Psalm 8 regarding humanity's dominion over creation and applies it christologically to Jesus.
Theological contrast: The order of creation and human dominion (1:26) meets God's judgment over that same creation (Zeph 1:3).
Direct narrative opposition: Creation in God's image (1:26) meets God's regret and destruction (6:7).
Restoration of the creation mandate: Human dominion is confirmed and expanded with fear after the flood.
Concrete exercise of the creation mandate: Humanity as the namer and ruler over animals (2:19) illustrates image and dominion (1:26).
Theological contrast: Human dominion over animals (1:26) is reversed to animal dominion over humans in judgment (Ezek 39:17).
Theological contrast: Humanity as God's image (1:26) meets a distorted likeness to God through sin (3:22).
Theological affirmation: God's sovereignty as Creator of heaven, earth, and humanity (Isa 42:5) underscores the foundation of the image of humanity (1:26).
Theological contrast: Humanity's dominion over animals (1:26) is reversed to the animals' dominion over humans in death (Jer 34:20).
Theological affirmation: God's sovereignty as Creator of the earth and humanity (Isa 45:12) underscores the foundation of the image of humanity (1:26).
